newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares end flat, awaiting foreign input.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares end flat, awaiting foreign input.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended barely changed on poor turnover on Wednesday and traders said future market direction was difficult to gauge.
The SBI index eased 0.46 points to 1,305.81, to take its losses to 2.3 percent in the last three days.

"The market is relatively optimistic due to a general expectation that foreign buying will resume in May, but investors are cautious -- being unable to say whether foreign interest will be large enough to support a rally," one trader said.

In February the central bank blocked foreign buying by demanding foreign investors open special custodian accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian shares.
The move triggered a bear run, sending the blue-chip SBI down 21 percent while average daily volume dropped to about 50 million tolars ($0.3 million) from 500 million previously.
"If foreign investors do not return by the end of May that could create a panic, which in the worst case could push the index down to some 1,100 points by the end of the year," an analyst said.
Turnover today fell to 46.6 million tolars from 54.4 million. Overall seven shares fell, five rose and 15 were untraded.
Issue A of drug producer Lek had the highest turnover, falling 0.73 percent to 24,600 tolars on volume of 622 shares for total turnover of 15.3 million tolars.
Mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska led the day's decliners, falling 3.22 percent to 1,801 tolars on volume of 3,862 shares for total turnover of 7.05 million tolars.
Food producer Droga was the top gainer, firming 1.50 percent to 27,000 tolars on volume of 282 shares for total turnover of 7.56 million tolars.
